item.title: The cost of being: A ‘formerly reckless, currently penny-pinching’ music writer
item.description: As part of our series exploring how New Zealanders live and our relationship with money, a writer with ‘no assets aside from a decent sense of humour and a positive attitude’ explains their financial outlook. Want to be part of The Cost of Being? Fill out the questionnaire here. Gender: Male. Age: 54. Ethnicity: Pākehā. Role: Music journalist, currently writing a book. One son, who’s out flatting and is about to finish uni. I live with my partner, who is the primary wage earner in our household.

item.title: Last call: Legendary K Road watering hole Charlie’s shuts its doors
item.description: Inside the final days of the famous bar – and what’s next for the family behind it. News that Charlie’s Bar was closing spread the old-fashioned way, through word of mouth – Karangahape Road is kind of like that. It spread fast and far enough that by its final day of service, the bar was packed with regulars and relics. Some drove all the way from Nelson, Tauranga and Whangārei for one last night out. item.title: From Jolene to Jonah: How pop culture influences New Zealand baby names
item.description: While parents may think deeply about what to call their offspring, name trends over the decades reveal the truth: we are deeply impacted by the names around us. item.title: The pitch deck generation
item.description: How kids hack tired parents with PowerPoint presentations to get what they want. Around three years ago, my then-nine-year-old daughter convened a formal “meeting” in the living room.
